name: The Server Renders Again
description: Acceptance-gate deliverable for the editorial-mono Pack — a cool, modern newspaper clipping authored FOR the editorial-mono dress, not a Syntax pack-flip. Doubles as the structural re-skin proof for the Pack→pixel epic: the card carries NO hard-offset shadow (editorial-mono newspaper.depth:'none'), where the same newspaper Surface under syntax carries the 12px zine shadow — a Pack changing STRUCTURE, not just colour, in pixels. INTENTIONAL deviations from Syntax aesthetic.md (which is Syntax-specific; editorial-mono has no aesthetic doc — it is defined by its manifest), carried here so the Critic does not re-flag them as aesthetic-miss: (a) hard-offset shadow intentionally absent — the flat structural re-skin; (b) cool palette (substrate #e9eef3, ink #0f151c, cyan accent #22d3ee) vs Syntax warm cream/yellow, all Pack-resolved; (c) the washi tape is a cool slate #aab9c9 carrying the Pack's cool-cast grain (editorial-mono washi-tape.grain-* override), not Syntax's yellow collage tape; (d) paper-grain warmth lowered to 0.1 for neutral/cool grit; (e) the mono signature thread is satisfied editorially by the mono kicker + byline + dateline, not a watermark; (f) registration jitter / torn edge n/a — clean printed clipping. Motion is restrained by design (settled-place + tape-down + a single underline stroke-draw; no halo-bloom or brightness-reveal — the latter is reserved for spoken-content text) — editorial-mono is the calm counterpart to Syntax's collage energy. Critic-ACCEPTed (no pipeline-bug / default-too-permissive). Acknowledged non-gating findings: the title:body cap-height ratio (~2.7) runs just over G4-density's 2.5 ceiling — emergent from the shared newspaper title-size default with the title already at its 4-slot minimum (same pipeline as the accepted title-card-newspaper), not preset-tunable; the underline ease is 'sharp' per G7's news-content assignment (a decisive, non-bouncy editorial mark), not the pack's default settled curve.

content.title: The Server Renders Again
content.author: BY M. OKONKWO
content.body:
For a decade the browser was the computer, and every serious application shipped a megabyte of JavaScript to prove it. That consensus is [underline]quietly unwinding[/underline].

The newest frameworks render on the server, stream HTML to the page, and treat client-side state as the exception. Nobody declared the single-page app dead — teams noticed their pages loaded faster, and stopped arguing.
